title: Automated compatibility matrix and staleness policy for Redwood-verified performance profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The current Redwood-verified performance profile catalog is manually curated and lacks a machine-readable compatibility matrix. This causes stale or incorrect profile recommendations when models are retargeted to new runtimes, quantizations, or hardware. Teams spend time manually re-verifying profiles and customers occasionally get suboptimal default pins.

Goal: Build an automated compatibility matrix generator and a staleness policy that together drive automated re-verification and profile lifecycle transitions (active -> stale -> deprecated). The system should integrate with the verification runner, profile catalog, and release gating to enable safe automated profile updates and clear operator visibility.

Outcomes: (1) A canonical, queryable compatibility matrix that maps model-version x runtime-variant -> expected performance bands and supported feature flags (quantization, KV cache behavior, seq-len caps). (2) A documented staleness policy with triggers and SLOs for re-run frequency. (3) Implementation of the automation that marks profiles stale and enqueues re-verification jobs, with operator override paths and audit trail.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix exists as a machine-readable artifact (JSON/CSV) and is stored/versioned in the profile catalog
Automated job enqueues re-verification when a trigger fires (model push, runtime kernel change, infra region rollout, or scheduled staleness interval)
Profiles transition states automatically (active -> stale -> needs-reverify) and those transitions are visible in Console catalog UI
Default model pins in the API consult the matrix and prefer verified active profiles; fallback behavior is documented and tested
Operator can manually mark profiles approved/skip-reverify; all actions are audited with links to verification runs and PRs
work_notes: 2026-02-15: Ticket created during PM sync. Problem statement drafted; initial scope agreed with Eng and RD team.

2026-02-20: Spike assigned to ENG infra team to prototype matrix schema and gather candidate attributes (model_arch, quantization, hw_family, kernel_tag, seq_len_limits, batch_recommendation, latency_p50/p95 bands, tokens_per_sec). Jonah to lead spike.

2026-02-28: Spike results: prototype schema stored as a git-backed JSON in profile-catalog repo. Verified 45 models across 3 hardware classes. Observed variability in kernel_tag semantics between runtime-1.18 and runtime-1.19 that requires normalization mapping.
2026-03-03: Design review with Console PMs: proposed UI changes to surface 'staleness' and last-verified timestamps. Agreed to add a quick filter for 'stale > 30d'.

2026-03-06: Blocker found: metrics ingestion pipeline (ingest-run-metrics) drops per-batch throughput for quantized kernels when seq_len > 1024. SRE investigating; temporary mitigation is to have re-verification jobs run with enforced seq_len sampling to avoid noisy tails.

2026-03-09: Prototype automation installed in staging: changes to verification-runner to emit compatibility-matrix entries after each run; catalog update PR opened: github.com/redwood/profile-catalog/pull/321. Need CI approval and e2e tests.

2026-03-10: In-progress: e2e tests flake due to timing sensitivity in continuous batching metrics. Working with runtime team to add deterministic token generation seeds for synthetic traces used in verification runs.
decisions: Keep the matrix schema intentionally minimal: only include attributes required for selection and fallback decisions (model_id, model_version, hardware_class, kernel_tag, quantization, seq_len_cap, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, throughput_tps, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd). Extra telemetry will be linked by run_id rather than embedded.
Staleness tiers: 'active' (last verified < 30 days), 'aging' (30-90 days), 'stale' (>90 days) with automated reverify enqueue in 'aging' and prioritized re-run for 'stale' profiles.

Verification thresholds: allow up to 10% relative p95 regression versus last verified band before flagging for manual triage; larger regressions trigger automatic rollback of default pin and customer-impact alert.
Automated changes to default pins require 'canary pass' in a small traffic cohort and post-deploy verification metrics; otherwise, change remains in catalog as non-default until manual promotion.
risks: False positives from noisy verification runs could cause unnecessary profile churn—mitigation: require 3-run rolling median before state transition.
Operator overload if many profiles enter aging simultaneously after infra kernel update—mitigation: rate-limit automatic re-verification and surface prioritization (high customer_impact first).
Edge cases where quantized kernels produce nondeterministic traces—coordination required with runtime team to stabilize synthetic trace harness.
notes_for_engineering: Schema to be backwards compatible; include a schema_version field in matrix entries
Verification-runner must emit 'run_id' and 'artifact_url' for each matrix entry
Add CI job that validates matrix consistency on PRs to profile-catalog
Provide a Console API endpoint /catalog/compatibility-query that returns best-matching active profile given (model_id, model_version, region, hardware_class, quantization_preference)
Include audit log entries for automatic state transitions with links to verification runs and metrics dashboards
